conclusion: The dispute between the two contested-criteria designs is adjudicated on the only ground truth the release offers: 365 of 3899 coval_core criteria (9.4%) have a verbatim twin in coval_full criterion, so for those, retention is a fact rather than a proxy. Among the 5,564 full criteria with at least 4 raters, 340 were copied; 10.9% of the copied are contested against 43.0% of the not-copied. Adjusted -- logistic on contestedness with |mean rating|, log rater count and the criterion's own across-response discriminability, cluster-bootstrapped over 986 prompts at 4000 fits over 5 seeds -- contested carries OR 0.3164 [0.1958, 0.4786], p 0.0002, while |mean rating| carries OR 1.5379 [1.3188, 1.8055]. A within-prompt permutation of the outcome puts the contested coefficient at -0.0618 (sd 0.1461), and the observed value sits -7.46 sd from it. WORLD: W-DISAGREEMENT-PENALISED. Disagreement costs a criterion its place even after the release's own stated selection signal is adjusted for, so the second design is right on ground truth. STRUCTURAL LIMIT, stated rather than argued away: verbatim copying is ONE retention pathway and 92% of core is rewritten rather than copied. If contested criteria are retained at the same rate but preferentially by rewriting, this design would read a change of pathway as a drop. That limit cuts identically for both disputants, and it is the only ground truth available.
